The drawers of index cards that libraries kept from the late 1800s until online catalogs replaced them in the 1980s and 1990s.

## Several cards per book

A book got one card per access point: one under the author, one under the title, one under each subject heading. The book itself sat in one place on the shelf, at its [[dewey-decimal-classification]] number, but the catalog let a reader reach it from several directions.

## Standard size

Cards were standardised at 7.5 by 12.5 cm, so drawers, typewriters and printed card services could all assume one format. Libraries kept these drawers up to date by hand for about a century.

## What I said reading it

The shelf is the one place; the catalog is how libraries got around the one place.
